summary: GET /users items gain latestOrder: the user's newest order or null. The page keeps a constant number of queries whatever its size.

acceptance.text: Each GET /users item has latestOrder {id, totalMinor, status, createdAt}: that user's newest order by createdAt (a tie: the higher id), or null when the user has no orders

Constant query count: GET /users runs the same number of queries whatever the page size (test/users.e2e-spec.ts 'GET /users runs the same number of queries whatever the page size' stays green, unchanged)
GET /users pagination (cursor, limit default 20, max 100) and GET /users/:id answer as before

tasks.title: latestOrder on GET /users items
steps: In src/users/users.service.spec.ts add the unit test "list returns each user's latestOrder": UsersService.list gives each item latestOrder, the user's newest order or null. It fails now: list() returns no latestOrder
In UsersService.list add latestOrder to each item: the user's newest order (createdAt desc, then id desc) as {id, totalMinor, status, createdAt}, or null
In src/users/users.dto.ts add LatestOrderDto and a list item DTO (UserDto plus a nullable latestOrder) for UserPageDto.data; GET /users/:id keeps UserDto
Run npm run typecheck and npm test: green

facts: src/users/users.service.ts: UsersService.list runs one user.findMany per page (select id, email, name, nickname; pageArgs + toPage)
test/users.e2e-spec.ts: 'GET /users runs the same number of queries whatever the page size' compares limit=5 and limit=50 through test/utils/query-counter.ts
src/common/pagination.ts: pageArgs fetches limit + 1 rows; toPage cuts the page and sets nextCursor

decisions.text: latestOrder = the newest order by createdAt, a tie broken by the higher id
Only GET /users items gain latestOrder; GET /users/:id keeps UserDto
No schema change and no new index: Order(userId, createdAt) exists
